steps.say: A cystic hygroma is a spongy neck swelling that has been present since birth in half the children who carry one. It arises from the jugular sacs and usually sits behind the neck, though the armpit and groin can harbour one. Most remain soft and painless until they bleed.
steps.tx: **Cystic hygroma** (multiloculated lymphatic swelling) is an endothelial lined **lymphatic malformation** (faulty lymph channels) of the **jugular sac** (neck lymph pouch), usually posterior neck, with about **50** percent present at birth. Other sites are axilla, mediastinum, groin and retroperitoneum, and the mass feels soft until complications strike.

steps.say: A huge neck mass seen before birth can block the first breath, so delivery becomes a planned rescue. Fetal ultrasound with fetal magnetic resonance maps the extent and shows how the airway is pushed. The EXIT procedure then holds the placenta working while surgeons secure the airway.
steps.tx: A large fetal neck mass threatens the airway at birth, and prenatal ultrasound with **fetal magnetic resonance** (womb MRI mapping extent) defines mass effect. An **ex utero intrapartum treatment** (EXIT procedure, securing the airway on placental support) prevents fatal **airway obstruction** (blocked newborn breathing) at delivery.

nodes.label: Fetal scan shows large neck mass
Fetal magnetic resonance maps airway push
EXIT procedure secures airway at birth

steps.say: These swellings bleed without warning and pick up infections easily, so disappearing lumps still need imaging. Magnetic resonance imaging traces every lymphatic channel before the operation. Complete excision with tedious ligation of branches remains the standard, since blunt or cautery dissection invites recurrence.
steps.tx: Cystic hygromas suffer **hemorrhage** (sudden bleeding into the cyst) and infection, and **magnetic resonance imaging** (MRI tracing lymphatic channels) plans the operation. Surgery demands **complete excision** (removing every loculation) with tedious ligation of branches, because blunt or cautery dissection causes recurrence and infection.

steps.say: Some hygromas wrap around nerves and vessels that cannot be sacrificed, and chasing them would cripple the child. Sclerotherapy then shrinks the swelling without a knife. Bleomycin, doxycycline and OK-432 from Streptococcus pyogenes all work well when injected into the cyst.
steps.tx: When **complete excision** (full removal) is unsafe near nerves and vessels, **sclerotherapy** (injected scarring medicine) is an effective nonsurgical option. **Bleomycin** (antitumour antibiotic sclerosant), **doxycycline** (tetracycline sclerosant) and OK-432 from Streptococcus pyogenes shrink the cyst from within. Needle aspiration alone fails because the cyst refills, so definitive sclerotherapy follows imaging.

steps.say: A painful swollen gland after a kitten scratch usually remains self-limited, so reassure the family and review only if it persists. Bartonella henselae causes this adenopathy of cat-scratch disease. Lymph node polymerase chain reaction confirms the germ and remains more specific than immunofluorescence.
steps.tx: **Cat-scratch disease** (self-limited painful adenopathy) follows **Bartonella henselae** (kitten scratch germ), and lymph node **polymerase chain reaction** (PCR copying germ DNA) confirms it. PCR beats immunofluorescence in specificity, and most children need only symptomatic care while nodes settle. Fever and a recent scratch support the diagnosis while the node remains tender and mobile.

nodes.label: Polymerase chain reaction on node sample

steps.say: A wobbly fluctuant node with dusky purple skin in a toddler points to atypical mycobacteria, not ordinary bacteria. Positive acid fast cultures with tuberculin skin testing support the diagnosis. Surgical excision cures the child, since medicines alone rarely clear these nodes and healing follows removal.
steps.tx: **Nontuberculous mycobacteria** (atypical germs) nodes turn fluctuant with **violaceous** (dusky purple) skin, and diagnosis rests on positive acid fast cultures with tuberculin skin testing. **Surgical excision** (removing the node) cures, because antibiotics alone seldom clear the infection. Incision and drainage are avoided because the wound heals poorly and leaves an ugly scar.

vis.alt: Child neck dissection showing a unilateral submandibular node with central liquefactive necrosis beside granuloma histology with bacilli.
vis.caption: Fluctuant nodes with violaceous skin and central necrosis need surgical excision for cure. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Ultrasound looks inside the node and tells you which child needs the operating list tonight. Nodes with central necrosis need urgent surgery before the skin breaks down. Fixed supraclavicular nodes with fever, weight loss or night sweats need malignancy workup including chest radiography.
steps.tx: Ultrasound detects nodes with **central necrosis** (dead liquefied centres) needing urgent surgery, while fixed **supraclavicular node** (collarbone nodes) disease with constitutional symptoms needs malignancy workup. **Chest radiography** (chest film) completes the screen for lymphoma or tuberculosis spread. Mediastinal widening or hilar nodes on the film further raise suspicion of lymphoma.

vis.alt: Paediatric lymph node examination map showing preauricular, cervical, axillary and epitrochlear stations with palpation technique.
vis.caption: Examine every station; fixed supraclavicular nodes with systemic symptoms need chest radiography. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Most viral neck swellings need patience rather than prescriptions, and parents welcome that news. Adenovirus, influenza and respiratory syncytial virus cause bilateral cervical nodes that fade with the cold. Reserve antibiotics for bacterial nodes, keeping surgery for necrosis or mycobacteria.
steps.tx: **Viral lymphadenitis** (bilateral cervical nodes from adenovirus, influenza or respiratory syncytial virus) needs **observation** (watchful waiting) only, while bacterial nodes need **antibiotics** (infection medicines). Surgery stays reserved for necrosis or mycobacteria, never for uncomplicated viral swelling. Bilateral nodes with runny nose and cough point to virus, and antibiotics are withheld.
